rationale: The first reply treated 'NN-H98' as a model series (NN-H984BF) and gave technician-level multimeter steps, which was a misread. After the customer clarified, it correctly read H98 as a microwave-output fault, advised against DIY, and eventually pointed to Panasonic service or an independent engineer. It was somewhat overconfident in naming the HV diode, capacitor or magnetron, and it wrongly said the code means 'high-voltage circuit malfunction' without noting the inverter. It also advised replacing the unit despite the customer saying they would pay for a sensible repair, and told them to try a reset they had already done.
